subject: Oceanography
title: Sonar
description: A short lesson to help you apply Sonar.

hook.text: Sonar lets us 'see' the ocean floor from a ship—by listening to echoes of sound bouncing off the bottom.

buildup.text: A transducer emits a sound pulse downward—the time for its echo to return reveals the water depth.

discovery.text: Multibeam sonar sends hundreds of beams at once—painting the seafloor in 3D strips as the ship moves.

twist.text: Side-scan sonar images the texture of the bottom—revealing shipwrecks, cables, and even individual rocks.

climax.text: Sonar revealed the mid-ocean ridge system—the longest mountain chain on Earth, entirely underwater.

punchline.text: Sound revealed mountains, trenches, and wrecks hidden by kilometers of water.

quiz.question: How does sonar measure ocean depth?
options: By timing echoes of sound pulses from the seafloor
